thread:
Alice: RFC follow-up: we keep debating who can flip the allow_broker_fallback / allow_org_exchange flags. We need a concrete approval flow + audit linking. Quick proposals?
Ben: Ops wants platform to own flips, but product teams need fast emergency access sometimes. Can't be manual every time.
Chandra: Proposal A: Platform + Security approval required for initial opt-in. After opt-in, service owners can request temporary emergency enable via infra portal with auto-esc to Platform if not approved in 10m. All requests must create an audit ticket ID.
Dmitri: Proposal B: policy-as-code only. Change manifest in repo: allow_broker_fallback=true + signed security approval label. No UI toggles. Emergency path via ephemeral approval token that expires in 30m. Logged and requires retrospective security review.
Elena: Tradeoffs: A is faster but increases operational surface. B is safer and auditable but slower for emergencies. We should combine: normal changes via PR (B), emergency via portal (A) with stricter logging and short TTL.
Ben: For emergency portal flow, require two approvers (service owner + platform oncall) and emit audit.event with ticket id. Also require a recorded reason and playbook link.
Chandra: Implement as policy-as-code with an infra-portal webhook: PRs create a change request, portal can fast-approve by creating a signed approval token stored in vault, which the runtime reads. That keeps audit trail and CI linkage.
Dmitri: CI gate: any PR that flips allow_broker_fallback must run shadow-eval and a small synthetic canary smoke test. PRs block merge until canary passes or unless security explicitly overrides with a reason.
Elena: Emergency token issuance flow should include: who granted, TTL (default 15m), justification text, related incident/ticket id, and an immediate notification to #eng-security. Also create a retention record for 90d.
Alice: Runbook entry: 1) If service needs emergency enable, open infra-portal request. 2) Portal requires service owner ack + platform oncall ack within 10m. 3) Portal issues ephemeral approval token -> runtime accepts short TTL toggle. 4) Post-incident create PR to policy-as-code to make it permanent if needed. 5) Security reviews and records findings.
security-bot: Policy note: default OFF. All opt-ins require platform+security sign-off. Emergency toggles are audited and auto-rollback after TTL.
Ben: Add metric: auth.broker.opt_in.count and audit.audit_tokens. Alert if opt-ins spike unexpectedly.
Chandra: Dev ergonomics: SDK should surface an error code EXCHANGE_DENIED with audit_id so clients can report the ticket link when paging.
Dmitri: We should also add automated suspicion detection: if a service uses emergency toggles >3x/month, auto-create a security review ticket.
Elena: Who owns implementing infra-portal webhook + vault storage? Platform. Who owns CI gating + canary? Devex + Platform. Security owns approval labels and policy review.
Alice: Action items: Dmitri to draft portal webhook spec, Chandra to add EXCHANGE_DENIED + audit_id in SDK, Ben to add metrics and dashboard, Elena & Security to finalize TTL and retention policy. PRs for policy-as-code layout by EOD.
infra-bot: FYI: infra-portal deploy scheduled for 2234567920. Watch infra-portal.canary.redwood.internal
Alice: Thanks all ":thumbsup:" tagging @oncall once PRs + runbook updated.
